description_full: CNB Financial Corporation operates as the bank holding company for CNB Bank that provides various banking products and services for individual, business, governmental, and institutional customers. The company accepts checking, savings, and time deposit accounts; and offers real estate, commercial, industrial, residential, and consumer loans, as well as other specialized financial services. It also provides private banking services; and wealth and asset management services, including the administration of trusts and estates, retirement plans, and other employee benefit plans, as well as a range of wealth management services. In addition, the company invests in debt and equity securities; sells nonproprietary annuities and other insurance products; and offers small balance unsecured loans, and secured loans primarily collateralized by automobiles and equipment, as well as engages in consumer discount loan and finance business. The company was founded in 1865 and is headquartered in Clearfield, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: CNB Financial Corporation is a small-cap financial services business with a $1.1B market cap on $282M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years and +12% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 11% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $59M in free cash flow — roughly 21 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.98× cash conversion.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.7%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 2.6% of the shares.
